## LECTURES

### [August 25, 27]{.in-person} Introduction to Population Health

-   Foundations of population health
    -   What is it?
    -   How it's measured, and
    -   What drives it.
-   Prevention, promotion, and protection; historical evolution of public health
-   Demographics: births and deaths
-   Presentation of the group project topics
-   Through case studies and group work, you explore determinants, disparities, and interventions from policy to individual care.
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/week1IntroPopHealth/)

### [September 1]{.in-person} Structural Foundations of Health

-   Why do some populations experience better health than others?
    -   social gradient
    -   structural inequities
    -   social context
    -   economic context
    -   environmental context
    -   housing
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/StructuralFoundationsHealth/)

### [September 3]{.in-person} Structural Foundations of Health (part 2)

-   Why do some populations experience better health than others?
    -   Policy & health
    -   Labor conditions
-   Community vs. population assessments
-   Group exercise
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/StructuralFoundationsHealth2/)

### [September 8]{.in-person} Population Health Theories and Frameworks

-   **QUIZ 1** (beginning of class)
-   **Groups formed, group project topics assigned, peer presentation pairings announced** — the first session after the add/drop deadline of September 4
-   Socio-ecological model
-   Life course perspective
-   Biopsychosocial model
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/populationHealthTheoriesAndFrameworks/)

### [September 10]{.in-person} Population Health Theories and Frameworks (con't)

-   Pathways from determinants to health outcomes
-   How do various determinants interact?
-   In-class exercise: identifying *moderators* and *mediators* on a causal pathway
-   **Assignment 1 due September 11**
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/populationHealthTheoriesAndFrameworks2/)

### [September 15]{.in-person} Measuring Health and Disease in Populations

-   Rates, ratios, proportions
-   Incidence and prevalence
    -   Population structure (age pyramids)
    -   Demographic changes: fertility, mortality, migration
    -   Preston curve: GDP vs. life expectancy
-   In-class exercise: age pyramids
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/measuringHealthAndDisease26)

### [September 17]{.in-person} Measuring Health and Disease in Populations (con't)

-   Demographic and health transition
-   Standardization in epidemiological research
-   Crude death rate
-   Standardized mortality rates
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/measuringHealthAndDisease26)

-   How to access health data

### [September 24]{.in-person} Measuring Health and Disease in Populations (con't)

-   In-class exercise: standardizing mortality between two counties
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/measuringHealthAndDisease26)

### [September 29]{.in-person} Measuring Health and Disease in Populations (con't)

-   Constructing life tables and deriving life expectancy
-   Potential years of life lost
-   Combining mortality and morbidity into DALYs

-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/measuringHealthAndDisease26)

### [October 1]{.in-person} Health indicators

-   **QUIZ 3** (beginning of class)
-   Disease classification
-   Death certificates, health surveys, hospital records, disease registries
-   Reliability and validity of different data sources
-   Health indicators and indices
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/health-indicators/)

### [October 6, 8]{.in-person} Peer Presentations

-   Each student presents **another student's community** (2--3 minutes)
-   **Slides due Monday October 5 at midnight** — whether you present Tuesday or Thursday
-   **Assignment 3 due October 7**

### [October 13]{.offline} Group work

-   Meet in groups in person or online
-   Divide the determinant levels among group members
-   Identify sources of prevalence (e.g. by county, state)
-   Gather and screen peer-reviewed sources
-   Plan the work leading to the checkpoint report

### [October 15]{.in-person} Epidemiological measures

-   **QUIZ 4** (beginning of class)
-   Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values of diagnostic tests
-   Screening trade-offs
-   Exercise: sensitivity and specificity among covid patients
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/epiMeasures/)

### [October 20, 22]{.in-person} Health Risk Assessment and Causation

-   **QUIZ 5** on October 20 — *last quiz before the midterm*
-   Causation
-   Risk Assessment and Bradford Hill
-   Measures of association: odds ratio, relative risk
-   **Assignment 4 due October 21**
-   **October 22: midterm exam review session**
-   [GITHUB Link](https://poph-001.github.io/causation)

### [October 27]{.exam} MIDTERM EXAM

-   **The entire class period — the full 75 minutes. There is no lecture that day.**
-   50 points, Chapters 1--5
-   **No notes, no cheat sheet, no devices**

### [October 29, November 5]{.in-person} Designing Population Health Studies

-   Validity, reliability, errors, bias and confounding
-   Confounding and bias in observational studies
-   *Midterm returned and reviewed in class on October 29*
